standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The decomposition of the product of the spectrum of a finite Galois extension with itself into the graphs of the elements of the Galois group

standard_prerequisites.name: The degree map is the pairing determined by the diagonal

core_obligations: Split the diagonal (proof lines 5067-5078): the product of the spectrum of the Galois extension with itself is the disjoint union of the graphs of the automorphisms, so the fundamental class of the product is the sum of the pullbacks of the class of the diagonal under those graphs, and the class of the identity is the corresponding sum.

Compute the pairing (proof lines 5078-5096): applying the map from the axiom defining the degree — which pairs with the class of the diagonal to one — to the displayed decomposition and using that pullbacks are compatible with this pairing gives that the value of that map on the identity is the number of automorphisms, that is the degree of the field extension.
Conclude (proof lines 5096-5100): since that map is the degree map of the spectrum of the extension, the assertion follows.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the diagonal of the product of the Galois extension into graphs of automorphisms.
Apply the defining map of the degree to the decomposition and count the automorphisms.
Identify that map with the degree map.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for data satisfying the first seven axioms the degree of the unit of the spectrum of a finite Galois extension is the degree of the extension (statement lines 5063-5068). The proof (proof lines 5069-5100) decomposes the diagonal of the product of the extension into the graphs of the automorphisms, applies the defining map of the degree, and counts. H2: a complete short computation.
